title: ICC issues arrest warrants for three South Ossetian officials over the 2008 war
body:
On 30 June 2022 the International Criminal Court issued its first arrest warrants in the Georgia situation, for three members of South Ossetia's de facto administration. They were Mikhail Mindzaev, the de facto internal affairs minister, Gamlet Guchmazov, head of the de facto Preliminary Detention Facility, and David Sanakoev, the de facto ombudsman. Human Rights Watch noted that the prosecutor's application also referred to Vyacheslav Borisov, a Russian major general who is now deceased.

The ICC approved warrants for unlawful confinement, torture, inhuman treatment, outrages upon personal dignity, hostage taking and unlawful transfer. The warrants concern the August 2008 international armed conflict between Georgia and Russia over South Ossetia. The ICC prosecutor had opened the investigation in January 2016.

Human Rights Watch said the suspects were believed to be in South Ossetian or Russian-controlled territory, that at least two held Russian nationality, which might make arrest harder, and that the ICC does not permit trials in absentia. It added that South Ossetian forces systematically destroyed ethnic Georgian villages after Georgian forces withdrew on 10 August 2008, and that it concluded they attempted to ethnically cleanse these villages. The conflict forcibly displaced tens of thousands of civilians, with the organisation citing nearly 20,000 ethnic Georgians forced from their homes. It was unclear whether the prosecutor would pursue cases beyond these three warrants.
